104	6. 105	7. The push credential is read from a mounted secret whose `items:` remap presents it as `config.json` under `DOCKER_CONFIG`.
106	8. `BUILD_TARGET=local` never touches a cluster: no Job is created, no kubeconfig is required, and the target works on a machine with no cluster credentials.
107	9. The Job is named `build-<TAG>`, lowercased and sanitised to a DNS-1123 name, so a run can be located by the tag it produced.
108	10. `upload` and `clean` print `nothing to do` and exit 0 when `BUILD_TARGET` is not `local` — otherwise a cluster build followed by `make clean` would `docker rmi` the unrelated local `1.3.0` image.

111	## Constraints
112	
113	- The local recipe's `docker build` arguments must not change: `--no-cache --rm=true --platform=linux/amd64 -t $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) .` stays, and no build args are added.

116	- `hack/build-job.yaml` must not live under a `k8s/` directory — a directory-scanned `make apply` would adopt it as deploy state. This repository has no `k8s/` directory today and must not gain one for this file.
117	- The Job image is referenced by digest, not by a floating tag.
118	- No new runtime dependency in the built image. This change is build tooling only.
119	- The local path must work with no kubeconfig and no cluster credentials present.
120	- `docs/dod.md`'s "`make build` succeeds" is a host-side check: the dark-factory container has no Docker daemon, so a prompt must not treat its inability to run `docker build` as a failure. `make -n build` and the `bash -n` checks are the container-executable substitutes.

123	- The five `hack/` files are copied from the pinned refs with their comments and hardening intact; the repository-specific values (image, repo URL) come from the Makefile environment, not from edits to the scripts. One inherited comment in `build-job.yaml` refers to a release-to-image dispatcher this repo does not have — that inaccuracy is accepted rather than edited, to keep the copy byte-faithful.
124	- **Reference**: the canonical procedure is `bborbe/go-skeleton` `docs/build-migration-guide.md` at `eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca`. This repo deliberately diverges in two places — the local arm stays plain `docker build` (the guide mandates `buildx` with `rewrite-timestamp`), and `VERSION` keeps `?= 1.3.0` (the guide has no default). A prompt must not "correct" either divergence.
125	
126	## Failure Modes
127	
128	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
129	|---|---|---|
130	| `BUILD_TARGET` names a cluster alias with no kubeconfig file | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero naming the missing file; no Job is created | Provision the kubeconfig, or use `sun` / `nukedev` / `nukeprod` |
131	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown target | `build-cluster.sh` dies at its context check with `unknown BUILD_TARGET '<x>'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod <contexts>`; no cluster call is made and no Job is created | Rerun with `sun`, `nukedev` or `nukeprod` |
132	| The cluster is unreachable | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero at the existence probe, carrying kubectl's connection error; no partial Job is left | Rerun when the cluster is available; `kubectl<wrapper> get ns build` confirms it |
133	| The Job is rejected at admission (pod-security, RBAC) | The make target prints the Job's events and exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe job build-<TAG>` shows no `FailedCreate` after the fix |
134	| The `build` namespace or `buildkit-push` secret is missing | The Job is created but its pod cannot mount the secret and never starts | Run `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>` once, then rerun the build |
135	| The git clone fails in the init container | The Job fails; its log names the ref and the git error | Correct `REF`, or verify the ref exists on the remote |
136	| The cluster resolves `REF` to a different commit than the local repository | The build container refuses before building: `REF <ref> is commit epoch <x> in the cluster but <y> in the local repository` | Run `git fetch` locally and rerun |
137	| The registry throttles the push | The Job fails at the push with a `429` in its log | Wait and rerun; the Job is idempotent per tag |
138	| The registry push is refused | The Job fails at the push; its log carries the registry error | Verify the mounted secret and its `items:` remap, then rerun |
139	| A Job with the same name already exists | `build-cluster.sh` refuses before applying and names the delete command | Delete the old Job, or use a different `VERSION` |
140	| The Job exceeds its deadline | The make target fails and names the deadline it waited | Raise `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, or investigate why the build stalled |
141	| The build node cannot schedule the pod (request capacity) | The pod stays `Pending` and the Job hits its deadline; the make target exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe pod -l job-name=build-<TAG>` shows the scheduling event; free capacity or lower the request |
142	| `make build` is interrupted mid-wait | The Job continues in the cluster; a later `kubectl<wrapper> get job build-<TAG>` reports its state | Read the Job's state, or delete it explicitly |
143	
144	## Security / Abuse
145	
146	- The push credential exists only as a cluster secret, mounted into the build pod. It is never written to the invoking machine, never passed as a make variable, and never printed.
147	- `hack/build-cluster.sh` whitelists every value it substitutes into the manifest and rejects embedded newlines before rendering, so a crafted `REF`, `TAG` or `IMAGE` cannot inject YAML or shell.
148	- The `items:` remap is load-bearing: without it the secret file keeps its own name while Docker looks for `config.json`, and auth fails in the same shape a missing credential produces.
149	- `buildctl-daemonless.sh` runs rootless with `--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`. No privileged pod, no host namespace, no Docker socket.
150	- The init container sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and drops all capabilities; the build container carries no cluster credentials and cannot create, read or modify other resources.
151	- `REF` is passed as a clone argument, not interpolated into a shell string, so a crafted ref cannot execute commands in the init container.
152	
153	## Suggested Decomposition
154	
155	**One prompt, deliberately.** The whole change is five static files copied verbatim plus one Makefile branch; splitting it produced four prompts whose commits were each discarded by dark-factory's post-execution `FetchBranch` step under `workflow: worktree` (see `# Progress` on the task). A single prompt has no second fetch to fail on.
156	
157	| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
158	|---|---|---|---|---|
159	| 1 | Copy the five `hack/` files verbatim from the pinned refs, add the `BUILD_TARGET` selector + cluster branch + defaulted-`VERSION` guard to the Makefile, make `upload`/`clean` no-ops for a cluster target, and add the `## Unreleased` entry | 1–10 | 1–9 | — |
160	
161	**How the prompt obtains the bodies.** The prompt-creator runs on the host, not in the container. It reads each file at generation time with `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor show 91a7e64e160f30be8af0aea64635e1e11bc86731:hack/<file>` (and `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton show eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca:hack/<file>` for `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`) and inlines the content into the prompt body. The executing container must never be asked to reach either repository. If generation is ever containerised, the fallback is to land the five bodies under `docs/` in this repo first and have the prompt copy from there.
162	
163	**DB11 / AC10 (`precommit`, `test`) are already satisfied by a bootstrap commit** — the pipeline's preflight runs `make precommit` before any prompt container starts, so they cannot be created by a prompt. The operator-executable rung runs after merge, so no prompt depends on a cluster being reachable.
164	
165	## Do-Nothing Option
166	
167	`openldap`'s image keeps requiring this Mac. The repo stays in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout, the goal's per-repo evidence row cannot be written, and the release path keeps its single point of failure. The mirror and the StatefulSet keep pulling an image that can only be cut by hand on one machine.

## Problem

Every `bborbe` image build today runs `docker build` on whichever machine invokes `make build`. This repository's `Makefile` has a single `build` target with no selector, so its image can be produced on one Mac and nowhere else. That serialises the release on a machine that may be asleep or have its Docker daemon stopped, and it is why `openldap` sits in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout.

The deployment already depends on this image being reproducible elsewhere: `nuke/teamvault/k8s/ldap-sts.yaml:21,40` renders `${REGISTRY_HOST}/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0`, and that name is populated by nuke's mirror step from the `docker.io` image this build produces.

## Goal

`make build` with no `BUILD_TARGET` behaves exactly as it does today. `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<git-ref> VERSION=<tag>` creates a Job in that cluster which clones the ref, builds and pushes the image; the make target blocks until the Job reaches a terminal state and exits non-zero if it failed. The Job spec is one reusable, parameterized file at `hack/build-job.yaml` that nothing else in the repo adopts as deploy state.

## Non-goals

- Migrating any other repository. This is `openldap` only.
- Changing image naming, the `docker.io/bborbe/openldap` repository, or the local arm's `$(VERSION)` tag and its `1.3.0` default.
- Loading the built image back to the invoking machine (`--load`). Rejected, not deferred: it keeps the push credential on the local machine.
- Pushing to the in-cluster registries, and the nuke mirror pin bump in `nuke/base/Makefile:23`. The mirror stays a mirror.
- Multi-arch images. `linux/amd64` only, matching the cluster nodes.
- Provisioning cluster namespaces or credentials as a deliverable. `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` runs them, once, as a prerequisite.
- Release-time build triggering. That is a separate concern.
- A buildx Kubernetes driver path, a Kaniko path, or any second executor. One executor ships.
- Adding `BUILD_*` build args to the `Dockerfile`. It consumes none today and needs none.
- An `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` escape hatch. `agent-task-executor` ships one as a bypass of the defaulted-`VERSION` guard; this repo takes the guard without the bypass, so the refusal is unconditional.

## Assumptions

- The cluster aliases are `sun`, `nukedev` and `nukeprod`; `hack/cluster-alias.sh` maps them to `~/.kube/sun` (context `default`), `~/.kube/nuke-dev` (context `nuke-dev`) and `~/.kube/nuke-prod` (context `nuke-prod`). Any other value is treated as a plain kubectl context in the ambient kubeconfig.
- The `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` secret are provisioned once by `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>`; this spec does not create them and the Job cannot push without them.
- `crane`, `teamvault-cli` (with a Keychain login for the docker.io push account) and a `kubectl` wrapper for the target cluster are present on the operator's host.
- The target cluster can reach `github.com` and `docker.io`.
- The operator runs the cluster-arm evidence commands against the same cluster the Job was created in, named by the wrapper matching `BUILD_TARGET`.
- The scratch tag passed as `VERSION` is lowercase and DNS-safe, so the derived Job name equals `build-<scratch-tag>`.

- `make build && docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0` — the local arm still lands an image

**No scenario is added.** The operator rung above is the accepted end-to-end substitute: it runs the real cluster Job, reads its terminal state and node, resolves the pushed digest through `crane`, and asserts the image is absent locally — the four observations a no-op cannot fake. This repository has no scenario harness, and bootstrapping one to replay a proof the operator rung already performs is disproportionate.

## Desired Behavior

1. `make build` with no `BUILD_TARGET`, or `BUILD_TARGET=local`, runs the existing `docker build` recipe and leaves the image in the local Docker store under `docker.io/bborbe/openldap:$(VERSION)`.
2. `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` renders `hack/build-job.yaml` with the run's values, applies it to the cluster's `build` namespace, and blocks until the Job reaches a terminal state.
3. The make target exits 0 when the Job succeeded and non-zero when it failed, printing the Job's pod log tail on failure so the cause is visible without a separate `kubectl` call.
4. The cluster arm refuses a `VERSION` that came from the Makefile default (`$(origin VERSION)` = `file`), naming the missing explicit tag, and creates no Job.
5. The Job's git init container clones the requested `REF` — not the default branch — into an `emptyDir`, and derives `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from that commit. A ref that does not resolve in the local repository aborts the run before a Job is created.
6. The build container runs `buildctl-daemonless.sh build` with `--opt build-arg:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=<epoch>`, the `BUILD_GIT_VERSION` / `BUILD_GIT_COMMIT` / `BUILD_DATE` / `DOCKER_REGISTRY` build args, and `--output type=image,name=<IMAGE>:<TAG>,push=true,rewrite-timestamp=true`. This Dockerfile consumes none of those build args; they are passed and ignored.
7. The push credential is read from a mounted secret whose `items:` remap presents it as `config.json` under `DOCKER_CONFIG`.
8. `BUILD_TARGET=local` never touches a cluster: no Job is created, no kubeconfig is required, and the target works on a machine with no cluster credentials.
9. The Job is named `build-<TAG>`, lowercased and sanitised to a DNS-1123 name, so a run can be located by the tag it produced.
10. `upload` and `clean` print `nothing to do` and exit 0 when `BUILD_TARGET` is not `local` — otherwise a cluster build followed by `make clean` would `docker rmi` the unrelated local `1.3.0` image.
11. `make precommit` and `make test` exist and are container-safe: `precommit` runs `bash -n` over the three `hack/` scripts and `make -n build`, and neither target invokes `docker`. Both land in a bootstrap commit before any prompt runs — the pipeline's preflight executes `make precommit` before the prompt container starts, so a prompt that creates them is too late.

## Constraints

- The local recipe's `docker build` arguments must not change: `--no-cache --rm=true --platform=linux/amd64 -t $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) .` stays, and no build args are added.
- `VERSION`, `REGISTRY` and `IMAGE` keep their current definitions and meanings. `VERSION` remains the image tag and keeps its `?= 1.3.0` default on line 1.
- **The defaulted-`VERSION` guard must sit inside the cluster branch only.** `VERSION` is assigned in the file itself, so `$(origin VERSION)` reads `file` on every bare `make build`; a guard evaluated at parse time would refuse the local arm, which is the opposite of the intent. The copied `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` bypass is deliberately not carried over (see Non-goals).
- `hack/build-job.yaml` must not live under a `k8s/` directory — a directory-scanned `make apply` would adopt it as deploy state. This repository has no `k8s/` directory today and must not gain one for this file.
- The Job image is referenced by digest, not by a floating tag.
- No new runtime dependency in the built image. This change is build tooling only.
- The local path must work with no kubeconfig and no cluster credentials present.
- `docs/dod.md`'s "`make build` succeeds" is a host-side check: the dark-factory container has no Docker daemon, so a prompt must not treat its inability to run `docker build` as a failure. `make -n build` and the `bash -n` checks are the container-executable substitutes.
- **`make precommit` and `make test` are the pipeline's gates and both land in a bootstrap commit before any prompt runs.** `.dark-factory.yaml` leaves `validationCommand: make precommit` and `testCommand: make test` at their dark-factory defaults, and preflight executes `make precommit` *before* the prompt container starts. Both targets are therefore added up front and must stay Docker-free, since the container has no daemon.
- **No Go-specific plugin documentation.** This repo ships a `Dockerfile` and build scripts, not Go code. Prompts must not cite `coding/docs/go-makefile-commands.md` or any other language-specific plugin doc, and `make test` is intentionally a no-op rather than a test suite.
- The five `hack/` files are copied from the pinned refs with their comments and hardening intact; the repository-specific values (image, repo URL) come from the Makefile environment, not from edits to the scripts. One inherited comment in `build-job.yaml` refers to a release-to-image dispatcher this repo does not have — that inaccuracy is accepted rather than edited, to keep the copy byte-faithful.
- **Reference**: the canonical procedure is `bborbe/go-skeleton` `docs/build-migration-guide.md` at `eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca`. This repo deliberately diverges in two places — the local arm stays plain `docker build` (the guide mandates `buildx` with `rewrite-timestamp`), and `VERSION` keeps `?= 1.3.0` (the guide has no default). A prompt must not "correct" either divergence.

## Failure Modes

| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
|---|---|---|
| `BUILD_TARGET` names a cluster alias with no kubeconfig file | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero naming the missing file; no Job is created | Provision the kubeconfig, or use `sun` / `nukedev` / `nukeprod` |
| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown target | `build-cluster.sh` dies at its context check with `unknown BUILD_TARGET '<x>'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod <contexts>`; no cluster call is made and no Job is created | Rerun with `sun`, `nukedev` or `nukeprod` |
| The cluster is unreachable | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero at the existence probe, carrying kubectl's connection error; no partial Job is left | Rerun when the cluster is available; `kubectl<wrapper> get ns build` confirms it |
| The Job is rejected at admission (pod-security, RBAC) | The make target prints the Job's events and exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe job build-<TAG>` shows no `FailedCreate` after the fix |
| The `build` namespace or `buildkit-push` secret is missing | The Job is created but its pod cannot mount the secret and never starts | Run `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>` once, then rerun the build |
| The git clone fails in the init container | The Job fails; its log names the ref and the git error | Correct `REF`, or verify the ref exists on the remote |
| The cluster resolves `REF` to a different commit than the local repository | The build container refuses before building: `REF <ref> is commit epoch <x> in the cluster but <y> in the local repository` | Run `git fetch` locally and rerun |
| The registry throttles the push | The Job fails at the push with a `429` in its log | Wait and rerun; the Job is idempotent per tag |
| The registry push is refused | The Job fails at the push; its log carries the registry error | Verify the mounted secret and its `items:` remap, then rerun |
| A Job with the same name already exists | `build-cluster.sh` refuses before applying and names the delete command | Delete the old Job, or use a different `VERSION` |
| The Job exceeds its deadline | The make target fails and names the deadline it waited | Raise `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, or investigate why the build stalled |
| The build node cannot schedule the pod (request capacity) | The pod stays `Pending` and the Job hits its deadline; the make target exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe pod -l job-name=build-<TAG>` shows the scheduling event; free capacity or lower the request |
| `make build` is interrupted mid-wait | The Job continues in the cluster; a later `kubectl<wrapper> get job build-<TAG>` reports its state | Read the Job's state, or delete it explicitly |

## Security / Abuse

- The push credential exists only as a cluster secret, mounted into the build pod. It is never written to the invoking machine, never passed as a make variable, and never printed.
- `hack/build-cluster.sh` whitelists every value it substitutes into the manifest and rejects embedded newlines before rendering, so a crafted `REF`, `TAG` or `IMAGE` cannot inject YAML or shell.
- The `items:` remap is load-bearing: without it the secret file keeps its own name while Docker looks for `config.json`, and auth fails in the same shape a missing credential produces.
- `buildctl-daemonless.sh` runs rootless with `--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`. No privileged pod, no host namespace, no Docker socket.
- The init container sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and drops all capabilities; the build container carries no cluster credentials and cannot create, read or modify other resources.
- `REF` is passed as a clone argument, not interpolated into a shell string, so a crafted ref cannot execute commands in the init container.

## Suggested Decomposition

**One prompt, deliberately.** The whole change is five static files copied verbatim plus one Makefile branch; splitting it produced four prompts whose commits were each discarded by dark-factory's post-execution `FetchBranch` step under `workflow: worktree` (see `# Progress` on the task). A single prompt has no second fetch to fail on.

| # | Prompt focus | Covers DBs | Covers ACs | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Copy the five `hack/` files verbatim from the pinned refs, add the `BUILD_TARGET` selector + cluster branch + defaulted-`VERSION` guard to the Makefile, make `upload`/`clean` no-ops for a cluster target, and add the `## Unreleased` entry | 1–10 | 1–9 | — |

**How the prompt obtains the bodies.** The prompt-creator runs on the host, not in the container. It reads each file at generation time with `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor show 91a7e64e160f30be8af0aea64635e1e11bc86731:hack/<file>` (and `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton show eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca:hack/<file>` for `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`) and inlines the content into the prompt body. The executing container must never be asked to reach either repository. If generation is ever containerised, the fallback is to land the five bodies under `docs/` in this repo first and have the prompt copy from there.

**DB11 / AC10 (`precommit`, `test`) are already satisfied by a bootstrap commit** — the pipeline's preflight runs `make precommit` before any prompt container starts, so they cannot be created by a prompt. The operator-executable rung runs after merge, so no prompt depends on a cluster being reachable.

## Do-Nothing Option

`openldap`'s image keeps requiring this Mac. The repo stays in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout, the goal's per-repo evidence row cannot be written, and the release path keeps its single point of failure. The mirror and the StatefulSet keep pulling an image that can only be cut by hand on one machine.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Resolves BUILD_TARGET into the kubeconfig file and kubectl context that
# `kubectl` actually needs, and provides the kc() helper every call goes
# through. Sourced by hack/build-cluster.sh; keeping the mapping here rather
# than inline means any future caller shares it instead of restating it.
#
# Defines variables and a function only: no `set -euo pipefail`, no `exit`,
# no output. The sourcing script owns all of that.

# BUILD_TARGET is either a kubectl context in the default kubeconfig or one of
# the build clusters, whose contexts live in their own kubeconfig files under a
# name that differs from the one people use for the cluster. Resolve the alias
# into the kubeconfig file and context that kubectl actually needs; anything
# that is not an alias stays a plain context name. A case statement, not an
# associative array: macOS still ships bash 3.2.
KUBECONFIG_PATH=""
KUBE_CONTEXT="${BUILD_TARGET:-}"
case "${BUILD_TARGET:-}" in
sun)
	KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/sun"
	KUBE_CONTEXT=default
	;;
nukedev)
	KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-dev"
	KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-dev
	;;
nukeprod)
	KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-prod"
	KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-prod
	;;
esac

# Every kubectl call goes through this, so the resolved kubeconfig and context
# cannot drift between the validation and the calls it guards.
kc() {
	if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
		KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
	else
		kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
	fi
}
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Renders hack/build-job.yaml and runs it in the target cluster.
#
# Called from `make build BUILD_TARGET=<sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>`
# (Makefile.docker) with
# BUILD_TARGET, NAMESPACE, REPO_URL, REF, TAG, DOCKERFILE, IMAGE, PUSH,
# PUSH_SECRET and TIMEOUT in the environment. Not intended to be run by hand.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-job.yaml}"

NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
PUSH="${PUSH:-true}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3600}"
DOCKERFILE="${DOCKERFILE:-Dockerfile}"
DOCKER_REGISTRY="${DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"

die() {
	echo "build-cluster: $*" >&2
	exit 1
}

require() {
	local name="$1"
	[ -n "${!name:-}" ] || die "${name} is required; pass it on the make command line"
}

# BUILD_TARGET is resolved to a kubeconfig file and context by cluster-alias.sh,
# which also defines the kc() helper every kubectl call goes through.
source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"

# The equivalent invocation for messages the operator has to retype.
KUBE_HINT="kubectl --context ${KUBE_CONTEXT}"
[ -z "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] || KUBE_HINT="KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG_PATH} ${KUBE_HINT}"

require BUILD_TARGET
require REPO_URL
require REF
require TAG
require IMAGE
require PUSH_SECRET

# Values are substituted into the manifest with sed and land in shell scripts
# inside it, so each one is restricted to a whitelist before rendering. A value
# outside the whitelist is rejected, never escaped.
printf '%s' "${REF}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
	die "REF '${REF}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
printf '%s' "${TAG}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
	die "TAG '${TAG}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
printf '%s' "${IMAGE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
	die "IMAGE '${IMAGE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
printf '%s' "${REPO_URL}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]+$' ||
	die "REPO_URL '${REPO_URL}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]"
printf '%s' "${DOCKERFILE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
	die "DOCKERFILE '${DOCKERFILE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
printf '%s' "${PUSH_SECRET}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
	die "PUSH_SECRET '${PUSH_SECRET}' is not a valid Kubernetes secret name"
printf '%s' "${DOCKER_REGISTRY}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
	die "DOCKER_REGISTRY '${DOCKER_REGISTRY}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
printf '%s' "${TIMEOUT}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
	die "TIMEOUT '${TIMEOUT}' is not a number of seconds"
printf '%s' "${NAMESPACE}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
	die "NAMESPACE '${NAMESPACE}' is not a valid Kubernetes namespace name"
case "${PUSH}" in
true | false) ;;
*) die "PUSH '${PUSH}' must be true or false" ;;
esac

# `grep -qE '^...$'` matches when ANY line matches, so a value carrying a newline
# passes the whitelist on its first line and its remaining lines are injected
# verbatim by sed into the YAML and the embedded `sh -c` script. Reject embedded
# newlines for every value before rendering.

	case "${!_var}" in
	*$'\n'*) die "${_var} contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
	esac
done

# the cloned commit and the build container refuses to run on a mismatch.

fi

# the embedded `sh -c` script just like the rest.
case "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" in
*$'\n'*) die "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
esac

JOB_NAME="${JOB_NAME:0:63}"

JOB_NAME="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME}" | sed -e 's/[-.]*$//')"

rendered="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "${rendered}"' EXIT

sed \
	-e "s|__JOB_NAME__|${JOB_NAME}|g" \
	-e "s|__REPO_URL__|${REPO_URL}|g" \
	-e "s|__REF__|${REF}|g" \
	-e "s|__TAG__|${TAG}|g" \
	-e "s|__DOCKERFILE__|${DOCKERFILE}|g" \
	-e "s|__IMAGE__|${IMAGE}|g" \
	-e "s|__PUSH__|${PUSH}|g" \
	-e "s|__PUSH_SECRET__|${PUSH_SECRET}|g" \
	-e "s|__DEADLINE_SECONDS__|${TIMEOUT}|g" \
	-e "s|__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__|${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}|g" \
	-e "s|__DOCKER_REGISTRY__|${DOCKER_REGISTRY}|g" \
	-e "s|__NAMESPACE__|${NAMESPACE}|g" \
	"${TEMPLATE}" >"${rendered}"

# The rendered manifest, not the environment, decides the namespace. A template
# may hardcode `namespace:` instead of carrying the token, and polling the
# requested NAMESPACE would then watch a namespace the Job was never created in
# until the deadline expired.
#
# Anchored to the metadata block and stopped at the first match: an unanchored
# pattern would take a nested `namespace:` (a RoleBinding, a second document) as
# metadata, and `sed | head -1` can die on SIGPIPE once a second match exists.
rendered_namespace="$(awk '
	/^metadata:/ { in_meta = 1; next }
	in_meta && /^[^[:space:]]/ { exit }
	in_meta && /^[[:space:]]*namespace:/ {
		sub(/^[[:space:]]*namespace:[[:space:]]*/, "")
		print
		exit
	}
' "${rendered}")"
printf '%s' "${rendered_namespace}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
	die "rendered manifest has no valid metadata.namespace (got '${rendered_namespace}')"

# A kubectl failure must not read as "no such Job": an RBAC denial, a missing
# namespace and a bad context otherwise look exactly like an absent object, and
# the script would go on to apply.
#
# stdout is the existence signal and stderr is the diagnostic, kept apart: a
# warning on a *successful* `get` — kubectl prints a client/server version-skew
# warning on every server-contacting command — must not be read as an existing
# Job, or a healthy cluster refuses every build with a false message.
kubectl_err="$(mktemp)"
trap 'rm -f "${rendered}" "${kubectl_err}"' EXIT
if existing="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" --ignore-not-found -o name 2>"${kubectl_err}")"; then
	[ -z "${existing}" ] || die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} already exists; delete it with: ${KUBE_HINT} -n ${NAMESPACE} delete job ${JOB_NAME}"
else
	die "cannot read job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}: $(cat "${kubectl_err}")"
fi
rm -f "${kubectl_err}"

if ! kc apply -f "${rendered}"; then
	echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} was not accepted; events:" >&2
	kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get events \
		--field-selector "involvedObject.name=${JOB_NAME}" \
		--sort-by=.lastTimestamp >&2 || true
	die "could not create job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}"
fi

# 10# forces base 10: TIMEOUT is validated as digits only, but a value with a
# leading zero (0800) would otherwise be parsed as octal and abort the arithmetic.
deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 10#${TIMEOUT} + 120 ))
outcome=""
while [ -z "${outcome}" ]; do
	succeeded="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
	failed="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
	if [ "${succeeded:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
		outcome=succeeded
	elif [ "${failed:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
		outcome=failed
	elif [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "${deadline}" ]; then
		outcome=timeout
	else
		sleep 5
	fi
done

logs() {
	kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" logs \
		-l "job-name=${JOB_NAME}" --all-containers --prefix "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
}

fi

echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} ${outcome}; last log lines:" >&2
logs --tail=100 >&2
if [ "${outcome}" = timeout ]; then

fi

1	---
2	status: generating
3	approved: "2026-11-09T08:43:23Z"
4	generating: "2026-11-09T11:38:08Z"
5	branch: dark-factory/cluster-build-arm
6	---
7	
8	## Summary
9	
10	- `make build` gains a `BUILD_TARGET` selector. `local` — the default — keeps today's plain `docker build` invocation and its `$(VERSION)` tag. Naming a cluster instead renders a Kubernetes Job, applies it to that cluster's `build` namespace, waits for it, and reports the result.
11	- The Job clones the requested git ref, builds `linux/amd64` with rootless BuildKit, and pushes `docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<TAG>` using a credential mounted inside the pod.
12	- Five files land under `hack/`, copied verbatim from pinned source refs: `build-cluster.sh`, `cluster-alias.sh` and `build-job.yaml` from `bborbe/agent-task-executor@91a7e64e160f30be8af0aea64635e1e11bc86731` (v0.57.4); `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl` from `bborbe/go-skeleton@eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca` (3 commits after v0.8.3). The YOLO container mounts only this repository and `.dark-factory.yaml` declares no `extraMounts`, so the prompt must carry the file bodies inline rather than reach a sibling repo.
13	- `upload` and `clean` become no-ops for a cluster target — the cluster arm already pushed, and nothing was built on the invoking host.
14	- The local arm's observable behaviour is unchanged: same `docker build` arguments, same `docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0` tag, image present in the local Docker store.
15	
16	## Problem
17	
18	Every `bborbe` image build today runs `docker build` on whichever machine invokes `make build`. This repository's `Makefile` has a single `build` target with no selector, so its image can be produced on one Mac and nowhere else. That serialises the release on a machine that may be asleep or have its Docker daemon stopped, and it is why `openldap` sits in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout.
19	
20	The deployment already depends on this image being reproducible elsewhere: `nuke/teamvault/k8s/ldap-sts.yaml:21,40` renders `${REGISTRY_HOST}/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0`, and that name is populated by nuke's mirror step from the `docker.io` image this build produces.
21	
22	## Goal
23	
24	`make build` with no `BUILD_TARGET` behaves exactly as it does today. `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<git-ref> VERSION=<tag>` creates a Job in that cluster which clones the ref, builds and pushes the image; the make target blocks until the Job reaches a terminal state and exits non-zero if it failed. The Job spec is one reusable, parameterized file at `hack/build-job.yaml` that nothing else in the repo adopts as deploy state.
25	
26	## Non-goals
27	
28	- Migrating any other repository. This is `openldap` only.
29	- Changing image naming, the `docker.io/bborbe/openldap` repository, or the local arm's `$(VERSION)` tag and its `1.3.0` default.
30	- Loading the built image back to the invoking machine (`--load`). Rejected, not deferred: it keeps the push credential on the local machine.
31	- Pushing to the in-cluster registries, and the nuke mirror pin bump in `nuke/base/Makefile:23`. The mirror stays a mirror.
32	- Multi-arch images. `linux/amd64` only, matching the cluster nodes.
33	- Provisioning cluster namespaces or credentials as a deliverable. `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` runs them, once, as a prerequisite.
34	- Release-time build triggering. That is a separate concern.
35	- A buildx Kubernetes driver path, a Kaniko path, or any second executor. One executor ships.
36	- Adding `BUILD_*` build args to the `Dockerfile`. It consumes none today and needs none.
37	- An `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` escape hatch. `agent-task-executor` ships one as a bypass of the defaulted-`VERSION` guard; this repo takes the guard without the bypass, so the refusal is unconditional.
38	
39	## Assumptions
40	
41	- The cluster aliases are `sun`, `nukedev` and `nukeprod`; `hack/cluster-alias.sh` maps them to `~/.kube/sun` (context `default`), `~/.kube/nuke-dev` (context `nuke-dev`) and `~/.kube/nuke-prod` (context `nuke-prod`). Any other value is treated as a plain kubectl context in the ambient kubeconfig.
42	- The `build` namespace and the `buildkit-push` secret are provisioned once by `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>`; this spec does not create them and the Job cannot push without them.
43	- `crane`, `teamvault-cli` (with a Keychain login for the docker.io push account) and a `kubectl` wrapper for the target cluster are present on the operator's host.
44	- The target cluster can reach `github.com` and `docker.io`.
45	- The operator runs the cluster-arm evidence commands against the same cluster the Job was created in, named by the wrapper matching `BUILD_TARGET`.
46	- The scratch tag passed as `VERSION` is lowercase and DNS-safe, so the derived Job name equals `build-<scratch-tag>`.
47	
48	## Acceptance Criteria
49	
50	- [ ] **`BUILD_TARGET` defaults to `local` and the local recipe is unchanged** — evidence: `make -n build` with no `BUILD_TARGET` emits `docker build --no-cache --rm=true --platform=linux/amd64 -t docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0 .` as its only command line, and its output contains no occurrence of `hack/build-cluster.sh`.
51	- [ ] **The local arm still produces an image in the local Docker store** — evidence: after `docker rmi docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0`, `make build` exits 0 and `docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0` exits 0 printing a non-empty `sha256:` id.
52	- [ ] **The cluster arm refuses a defaulted `VERSION`** — evidence: `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<full-sha>` (no `VERSION` on the command line) exits non-zero, its stderr contains `the cluster arm needs an explicit VERSION`, and `kubectl<wrapper> -n build get jobs -o name | wc -l` is the same before and after the attempt.
53	- [ ] **Post-Deploy (Rung-3):** a cluster target creates a Job that completes and pushes — evidence: `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<full-sha> VERSION=<scratch-tag>` exits 0; `kubectl<wrapper> -n build get job build-<scratch-tag> -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}'` returns `1`; `kubectl<wrapper> -n build get pod -l job-name=build-<scratch-tag> -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}'` returns a non-empty node name; `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<scratch-tag>` returns a `sha256:` digest.
54	  - `deploy_check:` `kubectlsun -n build get namespace build -o jsonpath='{.metadata.name}'`
55	  - `deploy_target:` `build`
56	
57	  This check asserts the `build` namespace exists, not deployment freshness — the change ships build tooling and deploys nothing, so a pass here means the target namespace is present, never that a new build was deployed.
58	- [ ] **The pushed reference is the repository the deployment consumes** — evidence: the `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<full-sha> VERSION=<scratch-tag>` output contains `IMAGE='docker.io/bborbe/openldap'` and `DOCKER_REGISTRY='docker.io'`, and the digest recorded in the previous criterion resolves at exactly `docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<scratch-tag>`.
59	- [ ] **The cluster-built image is absent from the invoking machine** — evidence: `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<scratch-tag>` fails with `No such image`.
60	- [ ] **All five `hack/` files are present, parse, and carry the copied hardening** — evidence: `test -f` succeeds for `hack/build-cluster.sh`, `hack/cluster-alias.sh`, `hack/build-job.yaml`, `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl`; `bash -n` exits 0 for each of the three scripts; `grep -c 'contains a newline' hack/build-cluster.sh` returns ≥ 1; `grep -c 'rendered_namespace' hack/build-cluster.sh` returns ≥ 1; `grep -c 'automountServiceAccountToken: false' hack/build-job.yaml` returns ≥ 1; `grep -c 'safe.directory' hack/build-job.yaml` returns ≥ 1; `grep -c 'oci-worker-no-process-sandbox' hack/build-job.yaml` returns ≥ 1.
61	- [ ] **`upload` and `clean` are no-ops for a cluster target** — evidence: `make upload BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> VERSION=<scratch-tag>` exits 0 and its output contains `nothing to do`; `make clean BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` exits 0 and its output contains `nothing to do`.
62	- [ ] **`CHANGELOG.md` carries an `## Unreleased` section naming the change** — evidence: `awk '/^## /{print; exit}' CHANGELOG.md` prints `## Unreleased`, and `grep -A6 '^## Unreleased' CHANGELOG.md | grep -c 'BUILD_TARGET'` returns ≥ 1.
63	- [ ] **`make precommit` and `make test` exist and run without a Docker daemon** — evidence: `make precommit` exits 0 and `make test` exits 0 on a host where `docker` is absent or the daemon is stopped, and neither target's output contains `docker build`.
64	
65	## Verification
66	
67	### Container-executable (runs inside the YOLO container at prompt time)
68	
69	- `make -n build` — prints the unchanged `docker build` line and no `hack/build-cluster.sh`
70	- `make -n build BUILD_TARGET=nukeprod REF=<sha> VERSION=<scratch-tag>` — prints the `hack/build-cluster.sh` invocation with `IMAGE='docker.io/bborbe/openldap'`
71	- `bash -n hack/build-cluster.sh hack/cluster-alias.sh hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` — exits 0
72	- `test -f hack/build-cluster.sh -a -f hack/cluster-alias.sh -a -f hack/build-job.yaml -a -f hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh -a -f hack/dockerconfig.json.tpl` — exits 0
73	- `grep -c 'contains a newline' hack/build-cluster.sh` — returns ≥ 1
74	- `grep -c 'rendered_namespace' hack/build-cluster.sh` — returns ≥ 1
75	- `grep -c 'automountServiceAccountToken: false' hack/build-job.yaml` — returns ≥ 1
76	- `grep -c 'safe.directory' hack/build-job.yaml` — returns ≥ 1
77	- `grep -c '^BUILD_TARGET' Makefile` — returns ≥ 1
78	- `grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*hack/build-cluster\.sh' Makefile` — returns ≥ 1
79	- `awk '/^## /{print; exit}' CHANGELOG.md` — prints `## Unreleased`
80	- `make precommit` — exits 0 with no Docker daemon present
81	- `make test` — exits 0 with no Docker daemon present
82	
83	### Operator-executable (runs on the host after PR merge)
84	
85	`kubectl<wrapper>` means `kubectlsun` for `sun`, `kubectlnukedev` for `nukedev`, `kubectlnukeprod` for `nukeprod` — the wrapper pins the kubeconfig and context, and `--context` / `--kubeconfig` are refused by the operator's shim.
86	
87	- `make build && docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' docker.io/bborbe/openldap:1.3.0` — the local arm still lands an image
88	- `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<full-sha>` — refuses, naming the missing explicit `VERSION`
89	- `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster> REF=<full-sha> VERSION=<scratch-tag>` — a cluster Job runs to completion
90	- `kubectl<wrapper> -n build get job build-<scratch-tag> -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}'` — returns `1` (the Job carries `ttlSecondsAfterFinished: 86400`, so this resolves within 24 h of completion)
91	- `kubectl<wrapper> -n build get pod -l job-name=build-<scratch-tag> -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}'` — returns a node name
92	- `crane digest docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<scratch-tag>` — returns the digest the Job pushed
93	- `docker image inspect docker.io/bborbe/openldap:<scratch-tag>` — fails with `No such image`
94	
95	**No scenario is added.** The operator rung above is the accepted end-to-end substitute: it runs the real cluster Job, reads its terminal state and node, resolves the pushed digest through `crane`, and asserts the image is absent locally — the four observations a no-op cannot fake. This repository has no scenario harness, and bootstrapping one to replay a proof the operator rung already performs is disproportionate.
96	
97	## Desired Behavior
98	
99	1. `make build` with no `BUILD_TARGET`, or `BUILD_TARGET=local`, runs the existing `docker build` recipe and leaves the image in the local Docker store under `docker.io/bborbe/openldap:$(VERSION)`.
100	2. `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` renders `hack/build-job.yaml` with the run's values, applies it to the cluster's `build` namespace, and blocks until the Job reaches a terminal state.
101	3. The make target exits 0 when the Job succeeded and non-zero when it failed, printing the Job's pod log tail on failure so the cause is visible without a separate `kubectl` call.
102	4. The cluster arm refuses a `VERSION` that came from the Makefile default (`$(origin VERSION)` = `file`), naming the missing explicit tag, and creates no Job.
103	5. The Job's git init container clones the requested `REF` — not the default branch — into an `emptyDir`, and derives `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` from that commit. A ref that does not resolve in the local repository aborts the run before a Job is created.
104	6. The build container runs `buildctl-daemonless.sh build` with `--opt build-arg:SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=<epoch>`, the `BUILD_GIT_VERSION` / `BUILD_GIT_COMMIT` / `BUILD_DATE` / `DOCKER_REGISTRY` build args, and `--output type=image,name=<IMAGE>:<TAG>,push=true,rewrite-timestamp=true`. This Dockerfile consumes none of those build args; they are passed and ignored.
105	7. The push credential is read from a mounted secret whose `items:` remap presents it as `config.json` under `DOCKER_CONFIG`.
106	8. `BUILD_TARGET=local` never touches a cluster: no Job is created, no kubeconfig is required, and the target works on a machine with no cluster credentials.
107	9. The Job is named `build-<TAG>`, lowercased and sanitised to a DNS-1123 name, so a run can be located by the tag it produced.
108	10. `upload` and `clean` print `nothing to do` and exit 0 when `BUILD_TARGET` is not `local` — otherwise a cluster build followed by `make clean` would `docker rmi` the unrelated local `1.3.0` image.
109	11. `make precommit` and `make test` exist and are container-safe: `precommit` runs `bash -n` over the three `hack/` scripts and `make -n build`, and neither target invokes `docker`. Both land in a bootstrap commit before any prompt runs — the pipeline's preflight executes `make precommit` before the prompt container starts, so a prompt that creates them is too late.
110	
111	## Constraints
112	
113	- The local recipe's `docker build` arguments must not change: `--no-cache --rm=true --platform=linux/amd64 -t $(REGISTRY)/$(IMAGE):$(VERSION) .` stays, and no build args are added.
114	- `VERSION`, `REGISTRY` and `IMAGE` keep their current definitions and meanings. `VERSION` remains the image tag and keeps its `?= 1.3.0` default on line 1.
115	- **The defaulted-`VERSION` guard must sit inside the cluster branch only.** `VERSION` is assigned in the file itself, so `$(origin VERSION)` reads `file` on every bare `make build`; a guard evaluated at parse time would refuse the local arm, which is the opposite of the intent. The copied `ALLOW_DEFAULT_VERSION` bypass is deliberately not carried over (see Non-goals).
116	- `hack/build-job.yaml` must not live under a `k8s/` directory — a directory-scanned `make apply` would adopt it as deploy state. This repository has no `k8s/` directory today and must not gain one for this file.
117	- The Job image is referenced by digest, not by a floating tag.
118	- No new runtime dependency in the built image. This change is build tooling only.
119	- The local path must work with no kubeconfig and no cluster credentials present.
120	- `docs/dod.md`'s "`make build` succeeds" is a host-side check: the dark-factory container has no Docker daemon, so a prompt must not treat its inability to run `docker build` as a failure. `make -n build` and the `bash -n` checks are the container-executable substitutes.

One inherited comment in `build-job.yaml` refers to a release-to-image dispatcher this repo does not have — that inaccuracy is accepted rather than edited, to keep the copy byte-faithful.

A prompt must not "correct" either divergence.
125	
126	## Failure Modes
127	
128	| Trigger | Expected behavior | Recovery |
129	|---|---|---|
130	| `BUILD_TARGET` names a cluster alias with no kubeconfig file | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero naming the missing file; no Job is created | Provision the kubeconfig, or use `sun` / `nukedev` / `nukeprod` |
131	| `BUILD_TARGET` names an unknown target | `build-cluster.sh` dies at its context check with `unknown BUILD_TARGET '<x>'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod <contexts>`; no cluster call is made and no Job is created | Rerun with `sun`, `nukedev` or `nukeprod` |
132	| The cluster is unreachable | `build-cluster.sh` exits non-zero at the existence probe, carrying kubectl's connection error; no partial Job is left | Rerun when the cluster is available; `kubectl<wrapper> get ns build` confirms it |
133	| The Job is rejected at admission (pod-security, RBAC) | The make target prints the Job's events and exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe job build-<TAG>` shows no `FailedCreate` after the fix |
134	| The `build` namespace or `buildkit-push` secret is missing | The Job is created but its pod cannot mount the secret and never starts | Run `hack/build-cluster-bootstrap.sh <cluster>` once, then rerun the build |
135	| The git clone fails in the init container | The Job fails; its log names the ref and the git error | Correct `REF`, or verify the ref exists on the remote |
136	| The cluster resolves `REF` to a different commit than the local repository | The build container refuses before building: `REF <ref> is commit epoch <x> in the cluster but <y> in the local repository` | Run `git fetch` locally and rerun |
137	| The registry throttles the push | The Job fails at the push with a `429` in its log | Wait and rerun; the Job is idempotent per tag |
138	| The registry push is refused | The Job fails at the push; its log carries the registry error | Verify the mounted secret and its `items:` remap, then rerun |
139	| A Job with the same name already exists | `build-cluster.sh` refuses before applying and names the delete command | Delete the old Job, or use a different `VERSION` |
140	| The Job exceeds its deadline | The make target fails and names the deadline it waited | Raise `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, or investigate why the build stalled |
141	| The build node cannot schedule the pod (request capacity) | The pod stays `Pending` and the Job hits its deadline; the make target exits non-zero | `kubectl<wrapper> -n build describe pod -l job-name=build-<TAG>` shows the scheduling event; free capacity or lower the request |
142	| `make build` is interrupted mid-wait | The Job continues in the cluster; a later `kubectl<wrapper> get job build-<TAG>` reports its state | Read the Job's state, or delete it explicitly |
143	
144	## Security / Abuse
145	
146	- The push credential exists only as a cluster secret, mounted into the build pod. It is never written to the invoking machine, never passed as a make variable, and never printed.
147	- `hack/build-cluster.sh` whitelists every value it substitutes into the manifest and rejects embedded newlines before rendering, so a crafted `REF`, `TAG` or `IMAGE` cannot inject YAML or shell.
148	- The `items:` remap is load-bearing: without it the secret file keeps its own name while Docker looks for `config.json`, and auth fails in the same shape a missing credential produces.
149	- `buildctl-daemonless.sh` runs rootless with `--oci-worker-no-process-sandbox`. No privileged pod, no host namespace, no Docker socket.
150	- The init container sets `automountServiceAccountToken: false` and drops all capabilities; the build container carries no cluster credentials and cannot create, read or modify other resources.
151	- `REF` is passed as a clone argument, not interpolated into a shell string, so a crafted ref cannot execute commands in the init container.
152	
153	## Suggested Decomposition
154	
155	**One prompt, deliberately.** The whole change is five static files copied verbatim plus one Makefile branch; splitting it produced four prompts whose commits were each discarded by dark-factory's post-execution `FetchBranch` step under `workflow: worktree` (see `# Progress` on the task). A single prompt has no second fetch to fail on.

159	| 1 | Copy the five `hack/` files verbatim from the pinned refs, add the `BUILD_TARGET` selector + cluster branch + defaulted-`VERSION` guard to the Makefile, make `upload`/`clean` no-ops for a cluster target, and add the `## Unreleased` entry | 1–10 | 1–9 | — |
160	
161	**How the prompt obtains the bodies.** The prompt-creator runs on the host, not in the container. It reads each file at generation time with `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/agent-task-executor show 91a7e64e160f30be8af0aea64635e1e11bc86731:hack/<file>` (and `git -C ~/Documents/workspaces/go-skeleton show eb050aa20bb6194d8af7e47baf8880df789bd1ca:hack/<file>` for `build-cluster-bootstrap.sh` and `dockerconfig.json.tpl`) and inlines the content into the prompt body. The executing container must never be asked to reach either repository. If generation is ever containerised, the fallback is to land the five bodies under `docs/` in this repo first and have the prompt copy from there.
162	
163	**DB11 / AC10 (`precommit`, `test`) are already satisfied by a bootstrap commit** — the pipeline's preflight runs `make precommit` before any prompt container starts, so they cannot be created by a prompt. The operator-executable rung runs after merge, so no prompt depends on a cluster being reachable.
164	
165	## Do-Nothing Option
166	
167	`openldap`'s image keeps requiring this Mac. The repo stays in the un-migrated half of the build-cluster rollout, the goal's per-repo evidence row cannot be written, and the release path keeps its single point of failure. The mirror and the StatefulSet keep pulling an image that can only be cut by hand on one machine.

49	#!/usr/bin/env bash
50	# Resolves BUILD_TARGET into the kubeconfig file and kubectl context that
51	# `kubectl` actually needs, and provides the kc() helper every call goes
52	# through. Sourced by hack/build-cluster.sh; keeping the mapping here rather
53	# than inline means any future caller shares it instead of restating it.
54	#
55	# Defines variables and a function only: no `set -euo pipefail`, no `exit`,
56	# no output. The sourcing script owns all of that.
57	
58	# BUILD_TARGET is either a kubectl context in the default kubeconfig or one of
59	# the build clusters, whose contexts live in their own kubeconfig files under a
60	# name that differs from the one people use for the cluster. Resolve the alias
61	# into the kubeconfig file and context that kubectl actually needs; anything
62	# that is not an alias stays a plain context name. A case statement, not an
63	# associative array: macOS still ships bash 3.2.
64	KUBECONFIG_PATH=""
65	KUBE_CONTEXT="${BUILD_TARGET:-}"
66	case "${BUILD_TARGET:-}" in
67	sun)
68		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/sun"
69		KUBE_CONTEXT=default
70		;;
71	nukedev)
72		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-dev"
73		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-dev
74		;;
75	nukeprod)
76		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-prod"
77		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-prod
78		;;
79	esac

81	# Every kubectl call goes through this, so the resolved kubeconfig and context
82	# cannot drift between the validation and the calls it guards.
83	kc() {
84		if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
85			KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"

95	#!/usr/bin/env bash
96	# Renders hack/build-job.yaml and runs it in the target cluster.
97	#
98	# Called from `make build BUILD_TARGET=<sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>`
99	# (Makefile.docker) with
100	# BUILD_TARGET, NAMESPACE, REPO_URL, REF, TAG, DOCKERFILE, IMAGE, PUSH,
101	# PUSH_SECRET and TIMEOUT in the environment. Not intended to be run by hand.
102	set -euo pipefail
103	
104	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
105	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-job.yaml}"
106	
107	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
108	PUSH="${PUSH:-true}"
109	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3600}"
110	DOCKERFILE="${DOCKERFILE:-Dockerfile}"
111	DOCKER_REGISTRY="${DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
112	
113	die() {
114		echo "build-cluster: $*" >&2
115		exit 1
116	}
117	
118	require() {
119		local name="$1"
120		[ -n "${!name:-}" ] || die "${name} is required; pass it on the make command line"
121	}
122	
123	# BUILD_TARGET is resolved to a kubeconfig file and context by cluster-alias.sh,
124	# which also defines the kc() helper every kubectl call goes through.
125	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
126	
127	# The equivalent invocation for messages the operator has to retype.
128	KUBE_HINT="kubectl --context ${KUBE_CONTEXT}"
129	[ -z "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] || KUBE_HINT="KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG_PATH} ${KUBE_HINT}"
130	
131	require BUILD_TARGET
132	require REPO_URL
133	require REF
134	require TAG
135	require IMAGE
136	require PUSH_SECRET
137	
138	# Values are substituted into the manifest with sed and land in shell scripts
139	# inside it, so each one is restricted to a whitelist before rendering. A value
140	# outside the whitelist is rejected, never escaped.
141	printf '%s' "${REF}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
142		die "REF '${REF}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
143	printf '%s' "${TAG}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
144		die "TAG '${TAG}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
145	printf '%s' "${IMAGE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
146		die "IMAGE '${IMAGE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
147	printf '%s' "${REPO_URL}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]+$' ||
148		die "REPO_URL '${REPO_URL}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]"
149	printf '%s' "${DOCKERFILE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
150		die "DOCKERFILE '${DOCKERFILE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"

154		die "DOCKER_REGISTRY '${DOCKER_REGISTRY}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
155	printf '%s' "${TIMEOUT}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||

165	# passes the whitelist on its first line and its remaining lines are injected
166	# verbatim by sed into the YAML and the embedded `sh -c` script. Reject embedded
167	# newlines for every value before rendering.

194	# is derived here, after that loop runs, and is spliced into both the YAML and
195	# the embedded `sh -c` script just like the rest.
196	case "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" in

200	JOB_NAME="build-$(printf '%s' "${TAG}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -e 's/[^a-z0-9.-]/-/g')"

204	
205	rendered="$(mktemp)"
206	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}"' EXIT
207	
208	sed \
209		-e "s|__JOB_NAME__|${JOB_NAME}|g" \
210		-e "s|__REPO_URL__|${REPO_URL}|g" \
211		-e "s|__REF__|${REF}|g" \
212		-e "s|__TAG__|${TAG}|g" \
213		-e "s|__DOCKERFILE__|${DOCKERFILE}|g" \
214		-e "s|__IMAGE__|${IMAGE}|g" \
215		-e "s|__PUSH__|${PUSH}|g" \
216		-e "s|__PUSH_SECRET__|${PUSH_SECRET}|g" \
217		-e "s|__DEADLINE_SECONDS__|${TIMEOUT}|g" \
218		-e "s|__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__|${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}|g" \
219		-e "s|__DOCKER_REGISTRY__|${DOCKER_REGISTRY}|g" \
220		-e "s|__NAMESPACE__|${NAMESPACE}|g" \
221		"${TEMPLATE}" >"${rendered}"
222	
223	# The rendered manifest, not the environment, decides the namespace. A template
224	# may hardcode `namespace:` instead of carrying the token, and polling the
225	# requested NAMESPACE would then watch a namespace the Job was never created in
226	# until the deadline expired.
227	#
228	# Anchored to the metadata block and stopped at the first match: an unanchored
229	# pattern would take a nested `namespace:` (a RoleBinding, a second document) as
230	# metadata, and `sed | head -1` can die on SIGPIPE once a second match exists.
231	rendered_namespace="$(awk '
232		/^metadata:/ { in_meta = 1; next }
233		in_meta && /^[^[:space:]]/ { exit }
234		in_meta && /^[[:space:]]*namespace:/ {
235			sub(/^[[:space:]]*namespace:[[:space:]]*/, "")
236			print
237			exit
238		}
239	' "${rendered}")"
240	printf '%s' "${rendered_namespace}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
241		die "rendered manifest has no valid metadata.namespace (got '${rendered_namespace}')"
242	NAMESPACE="${rendered_namespace}"
243	
244	# A kubectl failure must not read as "no such Job": an RBAC denial, a missing
245	# namespace and a bad context otherwise look exactly like an absent object, and
246	# the script would go on to apply.
247	#
248	# stdout is the existence signal and stderr is the diagnostic, kept apart: a
249	# warning on a *successful* `get` — kubectl prints a client/server version-skew
250	# warning on every server-contacting command — must not be read as an existing
251	# Job, or a healthy cluster refuses every build with a false message.
252	kubectl_err="$(mktemp)"
253	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}" "${kubectl_err}"' EXIT
254	if existing="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" --ignore-not-found -o name 2>"${kubectl_err}")"; then
255		[ -z "${existing}" ] || die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} already exists; delete it with: ${KUBE_HINT} -n ${NAMESPACE} delete job ${JOB_NAME}"
256	else

269	# 10# forces base 10: TIMEOUT is validated as digits only, but a value with a

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Renders hack/build-job.yaml and runs it in the target cluster.
3	#
4	# Called from `make build BUILD_TARGET=<sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>`
5	# (Makefile.docker) with
6	# BUILD_TARGET, NAMESPACE, REPO_URL, REF, TAG, DOCKERFILE, IMAGE, PUSH,
7	# PUSH_SECRET and TIMEOUT in the environment. Not intended to be run by hand.
8	set -euo pipefail
9	
10	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
11	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/build-job.yaml}"
12	
13	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
14	PUSH="${PUSH:-true}"
15	TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-3600}"
16	DOCKERFILE="${DOCKERFILE:-Dockerfile}"
17	DOCKER_REGISTRY="${DOCKER_REGISTRY:-docker.io}"
18	
19	die() {
20		echo "build-cluster: $*" >&2
21		exit 1
22	}
23	
24	require() {
25		local name="$1"
26		[ -n "${!name:-}" ] || die "${name} is required; pass it on the make command line"
27	}
28	
29	# BUILD_TARGET is resolved to a kubeconfig file and context by cluster-alias.sh,
30	# which also defines the kc() helper every kubectl call goes through.
31	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
32	
33	# The equivalent invocation for messages the operator has to retype.
34	KUBE_HINT="kubectl --context ${KUBE_CONTEXT}"
35	[ -z "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] || KUBE_HINT="KUBECONFIG=${KUBECONFIG_PATH} ${KUBE_HINT}"
36	
37	require BUILD_TARGET
38	require REPO_URL
39	require REF
40	require TAG
41	require IMAGE
42	require PUSH_SECRET
43	
44	# Values are substituted into the manifest with sed and land in shell scripts
45	# inside it, so each one is restricted to a whitelist before rendering. A value
46	# outside the whitelist is rejected, never escaped.
47	printf '%s' "${REF}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
48		die "REF '${REF}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
49	printf '%s' "${TAG}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$' ||
50		die "TAG '${TAG}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._-]"
51	printf '%s' "${IMAGE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
52		die "IMAGE '${IMAGE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
53	printf '%s' "${REPO_URL}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]+$' ||
54		die "REPO_URL '${REPO_URL}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:@-]"
55	printf '%s' "${DOCKERFILE}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$' ||
56		die "DOCKERFILE '${DOCKERFILE}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/-]"
57	printf '%s' "${PUSH_SECRET}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9.]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
58		die "PUSH_SECRET '${PUSH_SECRET}' is not a valid Kubernetes secret name"
59	printf '%s' "${DOCKER_REGISTRY}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$' ||
60		die "DOCKER_REGISTRY '${DOCKER_REGISTRY}' contains characters outside [A-Za-z0-9._/:-]"
61	printf '%s' "${TIMEOUT}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
62		die "TIMEOUT '${TIMEOUT}' is not a number of seconds"
63	printf '%s' "${NAMESPACE}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
64		die "NAMESPACE '${NAMESPACE}' is not a valid Kubernetes namespace name"
65	case "${PUSH}" in
66	true | false) ;;
67	*) die "PUSH '${PUSH}' must be true or false" ;;
68	esac
69	
70	# `grep -qE '^...$'` matches when ANY line matches, so a value carrying a newline
71	# passes the whitelist on its first line and its remaining lines are injected
72	# verbatim by sed into the YAML and the embedded `sh -c` script. Reject embedded
73	# newlines for every value before rendering.
74	for _var in REF TAG IMAGE REPO_URL DOCKERFILE PUSH_SECRET DOCKER_REGISTRY TIMEOUT NAMESPACE; do
75		case "${!_var}" in
76		*$'\n'*) die "${_var} contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
77		esac
78	done
79	
80	if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ] && [ ! -f "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
81		die "BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}' needs the kubeconfig ${KUBECONFIG_PATH}, which does not exist"
82	fi
83	
84	# The accepted targets are the contexts the resolved kubeconfig knows about, so
85	# an unknown target fails here with the list instead of at apply time. The
86	# aliases are listed too: they are valid inputs without being contexts.
87	contexts="$(kc config get-contexts -o name 2>/dev/null || true)"
88	printf '%s\n' "${contexts}" | grep -qxF "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" ||
89		die "unknown BUILD_TARGET '${BUILD_TARGET}'; accepted values: sun nukedev nukeprod $(printf '%s' "${contexts}" | tr '\n' ' ')"
90	
91	# The build clock is the built commit's timestamp. It is rendered literally so
92	# the Job states the epoch it will use; the init container re-derives it from
93	# the cloned commit and the build container refuses to run on a mismatch.
94	if [ -z "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH:-}" ]; then
95		SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH="$(git log -1 --format=%ct "${REF}" 2>/dev/null || true)"
96	fi
97	printf '%s' "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" | grep -qE '^[0-9]+$' ||
98		die "cannot resolve REF '${REF}' to a commit in the local repository; run git fetch and retry"
99	# SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is the one substituted value the loop above cannot cover: it
100	# is derived here, after that loop runs, and is spliced into both the YAML and
101	# the embedded `sh -c` script just like the rest.
102	case "${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}" in
103	*$'\n'*) die "SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH contains a newline, which is not allowed" ;;
104	esac
105	
106	JOB_NAME="build-$(printf '%s' "${TAG}" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' | sed -e 's/[^a-z0-9.-]/-/g')"
107	JOB_NAME="${JOB_NAME:0:63}"
108	# Truncation can leave a trailing '.' or '-', which is not a valid DNS-1123 name.
109	JOB_NAME="$(printf '%s' "${JOB_NAME}" | sed -e 's/[-.]*$//')"
110	
111	rendered="$(mktemp)"
112	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}"' EXIT
113	
114	sed \
115		-e "s|__JOB_NAME__|${JOB_NAME}|g" \
116		-e "s|__REPO_URL__|${REPO_URL}|g" \
117		-e "s|__REF__|${REF}|g" \
118		-e "s|__TAG__|${TAG}|g" \
119		-e "s|__DOCKERFILE__|${DOCKERFILE}|g" \
120		-e "s|__IMAGE__|${IMAGE}|g" \
121		-e "s|__PUSH__|${PUSH}|g" \
122		-e "s|__PUSH_SECRET__|${PUSH_SECRET}|g" \
123		-e "s|__DEADLINE_SECONDS__|${TIMEOUT}|g" \
124		-e "s|__SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH__|${SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH}|g" \
125		-e "s|__DOCKER_REGISTRY__|${DOCKER_REGISTRY}|g" \
126		-e "s|__NAMESPACE__|${NAMESPACE}|g" \
127		"${TEMPLATE}" >"${rendered}"
128	
129	# The rendered manifest, not the environment, decides the namespace. A template
130	# may hardcode `namespace:` instead of carrying the token, and polling the
131	# requested NAMESPACE would then watch a namespace the Job was never created in
132	# until the deadline expired.
133	#
134	# Anchored to the metadata block and stopped at the first match: an unanchored
135	# pattern would take a nested `namespace:` (a RoleBinding, a second document) as
136	# metadata, and `sed | head -1` can die on SIGPIPE once a second match exists.
137	rendered_namespace="$(awk '
138		/^metadata:/ { in_meta = 1; next }
139		in_meta && /^[^[:space:]]/ { exit }
140		in_meta && /^[[:space:]]*namespace:/ {
141			sub(/^[[:space:]]*namespace:[[:space:]]*/, "")
142			print
143			exit
144		}
145	' "${rendered}")"
146	printf '%s' "${rendered_namespace}" | grep -qE '^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?$' ||
147		die "rendered manifest has no valid metadata.namespace (got '${rendered_namespace}')"
148	NAMESPACE="${rendered_namespace}"
149	
150	# A kubectl failure must not read as "no such Job": an RBAC denial, a missing
151	# namespace and a bad context otherwise look exactly like an absent object, and
152	# the script would go on to apply.
153	#
154	# stdout is the existence signal and stderr is the diagnostic, kept apart: a
155	# warning on a *successful* `get` — kubectl prints a client/server version-skew
156	# warning on every server-contacting command — must not be read as an existing
157	# Job, or a healthy cluster refuses every build with a false message.
158	kubectl_err="$(mktemp)"
159	trap 'rm -f "${rendered}" "${kubectl_err}"' EXIT
160	if existing="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" --ignore-not-found -o name 2>"${kubectl_err}")"; then
161		[ -z "${existing}" ] || die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} already exists; delete it with: ${KUBE_HINT} -n ${NAMESPACE} delete job ${JOB_NAME}"
162	else
163		die "cannot read job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}: $(cat "${kubectl_err}")"
164	fi
165	rm -f "${kubectl_err}"
166	
167	if ! kc apply -f "${rendered}"; then
168		echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} was not accepted; events:" >&2
169		kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get events \
170			--field-selector "involvedObject.name=${JOB_NAME}" \
171			--sort-by=.lastTimestamp >&2 || true
172		die "could not create job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME}"
173	fi
174	
175	# 10# forces base 10: TIMEOUT is validated as digits only, but a value with a
176	# leading zero (0800) would otherwise be parsed as octal and abort the arithmetic.
177	deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + 10#${TIMEOUT} + 120 ))
178	outcome=""
179	while [ -z "${outcome}" ]; do
180		succeeded="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
181		failed="$(kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" get job "${JOB_NAME}" -o jsonpath='{.status.failed}' 2>/dev/null || true)"
182		if [ "${succeeded:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
183			outcome=succeeded
184		elif [ "${failed:-0}" -ge 1 ]; then
185			outcome=failed
186		elif [ "$(date +%s)" -ge "${deadline}" ]; then
187			outcome=timeout
188		else
189			sleep 5
190		fi
191	done
192	
193	logs() {
194		kc -n "${NAMESPACE}" logs \
195			-l "job-name=${JOB_NAME}" --all-containers --prefix "$@" 2>/dev/null || true
196	}
197	
198	if [ "${outcome}" = succeeded ]; then
199		logs --tail=-1 | grep -E 'pushing manifest for|containerimage\.digest' || true
200		echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} succeeded"
201		exit 0
202	fi
203	
204	echo "build-cluster: job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} ${outcome}; last log lines:" >&2
205	logs --tail=100 >&2
206	if [ "${outcome}" = timeout ]; then
207		die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} did not finish within ${TIMEOUT}s (+120s grace)"
208	fi
209	die "job ${NAMESPACE}/${JOB_NAME} failed"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Resolves BUILD_TARGET into the kubeconfig file and kubectl context that
3	# `kubectl` actually needs, and provides the kc() helper every call goes
4	# through. Sourced by hack/build-cluster.sh; keeping the mapping here rather
5	# than inline means any future caller shares it instead of restating it.
6	#
7	# Defines variables and a function only: no `set -euo pipefail`, no `exit`,
8	# no output. The sourcing script owns all of that.
9	
10	# BUILD_TARGET is either a kubectl context in the default kubeconfig or one of
11	# the build clusters, whose contexts live in their own kubeconfig files under a
12	# name that differs from the one people use for the cluster. Resolve the alias
13	# into the kubeconfig file and context that kubectl actually needs; anything
14	# that is not an alias stays a plain context name. A case statement, not an
15	# associative array: macOS still ships bash 3.2.
16	KUBECONFIG_PATH=""
17	KUBE_CONTEXT="${BUILD_TARGET:-}"
18	case "${BUILD_TARGET:-}" in
19	sun)
20		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/sun"
21		KUBE_CONTEXT=default
22		;;
23	nukedev)
24		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-dev"
25		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-dev
26		;;
27	nukeprod)
28		KUBECONFIG_PATH="${HOME}/.kube/nuke-prod"
29		KUBE_CONTEXT=nuke-prod
30		;;
31	esac
32	
33	# Every kubectl call goes through this, so the resolved kubeconfig and context
34	# cannot drift between the validation and the calls it guards.
35	kc() {
36		if [ -n "${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" ]; then
37			KUBECONFIG="${KUBECONFIG_PATH}" kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
38		else
39			kubectl --context "${KUBE_CONTEXT}" "$@"
40		fi
41	}

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Provisions the cluster-side prerequisites for a remote build: the `build`
3	# namespace and the docker.io push secret the Job mounts. Idempotent — running
4	# it twice exits 0 and leaves exactly one namespace and one secret.
5	#
6	# Called by hand before the first `make build BUILD_TARGET=<cluster>` against a
7	# cluster. It deliberately creates no Job: jobs are per-build, rendered by
8	# hack/build-cluster.sh, which refuses to run when one already exists.
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
12	TEMPLATE="${TEMPLATE:-${SCRIPT_DIR}/dockerconfig.json.tpl}"
13	
14	BUILD_TARGET="${1:-}"
15	NAMESPACE="${NAMESPACE:-build}"
16	BUILD_PUSH_SECRET="${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET:-buildkit-push}"
17	
18	die() {
19		echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: $*" >&2
20		exit 1
21	}
22	
23	[ -n "${BUILD_TARGET}" ] || die "usage: $(basename "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}") <sun|nukedev|nukeprod|kubectl-context>"
24	[ -f "${TEMPLATE}" ] || die "template not found: ${TEMPLATE}"
25	
26	# The same -teamvault-config value `make apply` takes (Makefile.k8s). Defaults to
27	# the config the repo's own .envrc uses, so an operator who has teamvault-cli set
28	# up does not have to export anything.
29	TEAMVAULT="${TEAMVAULT:-${HOME}/.config/teamvault-cli/config.json}"
30	[ -f "${TEAMVAULT}" ] || die "teamvault config not found: ${TEAMVAULT} (set TEAMVAULT to override)"
31	command -v teamvault-cli >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
32		die "teamvault-cli not found on PATH; it resolves the lookup key in ${TEMPLATE}"
33	
34	# Shared with hack/build-cluster.sh so the alias mapping cannot drift between
35	# provisioning and building.
36	source "${SCRIPT_DIR}/cluster-alias.sh"
37	
38	# The rendered credential lives in a 600 temp file for the length of one
39	# `create secret --dry-run` and is removed on every exit path. It is never
40	# echoed, never logged, and never written into the repo.
41	RENDERED="$(mktemp)"
42	chmod 600 "${RENDERED}"
43	trap 'rm -f "${RENDERED}"' EXIT INT TERM
44	
45	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: cluster ${BUILD_TARGET} (kubectl context ${KUBE_CONTEXT})"
46	
47	kc create namespace "${NAMESPACE}" --dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
48	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: namespace ${NAMESPACE} present"
49	
50	# The lookup key comes from the template, so the template stays the single
51	# declaration of which TeamVault item and which registry this secret is for.
52	TEAMVAULT_KEY="$(sed -nE 's/.*"([A-Za-z0-9]{6,12})" \| teamvaultUser.*/\1/p' "${TEMPLATE}" | head -1)"
53	[ -n "${TEAMVAULT_KEY}" ] || die "no teamvaultUser lookup key found in ${TEMPLATE}"
54	
55	# teamvault-cli, not teamvault-config-parser: the parser takes its password from
56	# the config file, which holds only url and user, so it authenticates unprivileged
57	# and gets 403 on this item. The CLI reads the login from the macOS Keychain.
58	TV_USER="$(teamvault-cli username --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
59	TV_PASS="$(teamvault-cli password --teamvault-config "${TEAMVAULT}" --teamvault-key="${TEAMVAULT_KEY}")"
60	[ -n "${TV_USER}" ] && [ -n "${TV_PASS}" ] || die "teamvault returned an empty credential for key ${TEAMVAULT_KEY}"
61	
62	# docker.io's canonical auths key, per the template.
63	printf '{"auths":{"https://index.docker.io/v1/":{"username":"%s","password":"%s"}}}' \
64		"${TV_USER}" "${TV_PASS}" >"${RENDERED}"
65	unset TV_USER TV_PASS
66	[ -s "${RENDERED}" ] || die "failed to render ${TEMPLATE}"
67	
68	kc create secret generic "${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET}" \
69		-n "${NAMESPACE}" \
70		--type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson \
71		--from-file=.dockerconfigjson="${RENDERED}" \
72		--dry-run=client -o yaml | kc apply -f -
73	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: secret ${NAMESPACE}/${BUILD_PUSH_SECRET} present"
74	
75	echo "build-cluster-bootstrap: ready — make build BUILD_TARGET=${BUILD_TARGET}"
